Q: "New Vertical/Horizontal Document Group" in Visual Studio 2026? A:

Those two options, Window -> New Vertical Document Group and Window -> New Horizontal Document Group, have moved to Window -> Move in Visual Studio 2026.

  • Window -> New Vertical Document Group is now Window -> Move -> To New Tab Group Right
  • Window -> New Horizontal Document Group is now Window -> Move -> To New Tab Group Below

Q: Python UnboundLocalError when updating a variable from an outer function (closure) A:

count isn't local to the inc function, so nonlocal count needs to be added to be able to modify it:

def make_counter():
    count = 0

    def inc(step=1):
        nonlocal count  # add here
        if step > 0:
            count += step
        return count

    return inc

c = make_counter()
print(c())
print(c())
print(c())

Output:

1
2
3

Q: Draw Surface_mesh returned from convex_hull_3 A:

There is a problem in the CGAL basic viewer in the way the initial size of edges is computed.

In your case, this size is too big, explaining the big black rectangles.

You can either to not draw edges (press E key), or decrease the size of edges (press - key, possibly keep it pressed for a moment...).

Q: Override the ToString() method to return all data members A:

Simply do

public override string ToString() => $"{_name}, {_number}, {_date}, {_salary}";

From micorsoft documentations.

Q: How to list all file mapping handles in Win32(64)? A:

Far Manager plugin "ProcList" shows the list of handles. Look the source handles.cpp. You need to look at function

bool PrintHandleInfo(DWORD dwPID, HANDLE file, bool bIncludeUnnamed, PerfThread* pThread)

DWORD dwPID - inspecting PID, HANDLE file - is a handle to output text file.

Q: Can't seem to generate payloadcms types or importmaps A:

This happens because payload generate:types / payload generate:importmap load parts of the admin/UI dependency graph in a Node ESM process, and Node 22 can’t execute non-JS imports like .css/.scss. When something in that graph imports react-image-crop/dist/ReactCrop.css (or @payloadcms/ui SCSS), Node tries to treat it like a module and throws ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION.

What to do:

  • Best fix: make the CLI run with a Node loader that stubs style imports (server doesn’t need them). Example approach:

    • Add an ESM loader that intercepts .css/.scss (and ideally other assets) and returns an empty module.

    • Run Payload with NODE_OPTIONS="--loader ./scripts/ignore-style-loader.mjs" for the generate commands. - this that we did.

  • Practical script example (package.json):

    • generate:types: cross-env NODE_OPTIONS="--loader ./scripts/ignore-style-loader.mjs" payload generate:types

    • generate:importmap: cross-env NODE_OPTIONS="--loader ./scripts/ignore-style-loader.mjs" payload generate:importmap

  • Also important: don’t import payload.config.ts (or admin bundles like payload/dist/...) directly from your own Node scripts; let Payload load the config. Importing the config yourself is a common way to trigger these CSS/SCSS imports “outside of Payload’s bootstrap”.

In our repo, the working fix was exactly this: an ESM loader that ignores .css/.scss including query-string variants (like file.scss?something) and using it for the Payload CLI commands. If you want, paste your package.json scripts section and I’ll write the exact loader + script lines for your project.
